title: Three-month Nino 3.4 forecasts had lower May skill but no clear May error increase over November in 1981-2025
abstract: We compared three-month linear Nino 3.4 forecasts for May and November targets in 1981-2025. Fits used earlier target years only in a fixed NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 monthly record. May and November mean squared errors were 0.2564 and 0.2529 C squared. Their paired difference was 0.0034 C squared, with a 95% five-year block interval of -0.1322 to 0.1293. Thus, a higher May absolute error is uncertain. Skill against the training mean was 36.31% and 82.07%. The difference was -45.76 percentage points, with an interval of -68.09 to -26.98. November training-mean error was 3.50 times May error, so close absolute errors give different relative scores. Rolling training and a year-trend check retained the relative skill contrast. A six-month lead did not. This is a retrospective score audit of one linear surface-index model. It does not discover the spring barrier, identify a physical cause, or measure operational forecast skill. The package gives exact data, code, forecasts, draws, figures, and independent numerical checks.
